_comment: Elite CS612 Modbus register map. Addresses are not kept in code but managed only in this file.
An entry with address null means the address is not confirmed. The node refuses that function,
and the UI disables the related buttons. Once an address is confirmed, only this file needs to be filled in.
count is the number of consecutive registers to read / write; poses are in [X, Y, Z, Rx, Ry, Rz] order.
The current TCP uses the robot's own registers 384~389. 260~264 are input fields written by RCS
before a job starts (radius, thickness, probe coverage, EOAT type). The task writes nothing
there — it once overwrote the TCP and the next cell read the coordinates as the radius.
Write addresses are in the general-purpose registers (256~383) read by the robot task.
Jog and home moves use 30001 scripts, not registers, so they are not listed here.
kind is the unit conversion method. pose treats the first 3 as position and the last 3 as rotation,
angle treats all 6 as rotations. Joint angles are mrad on all 6 axes, so they are angle.
raw stores the value as an integer as is (no sub-unit decimals). work_area is
one of these — app_width/height/overlap are plain mm and scan_h is 0.1 mm.
scan_state (290~299) is the progress state written by the robot task. In order:
state, row_idx, rows, alive, zero_ok, finished, pitch, progress, progress2,
probe_error; a cell's scan is complete when state==5 && finished==1.
probe_error (299): 0 = OK, 1 = probe_c, 2 = probe_l, 3 = probe_r contact failed, 4 = arc length / radius is 0 —
written by the sensor versions pc_press/al_press/pr_press right before halt() (dus_init resets it
to 0). operator-ui watches it change, handles the alarm and sends MQTT
evt/error (erut_session.raise_error path, see app.py).
home_flag (276) tells whether the robot is at home (1 home, 0 away). The task's publishing thread
compares the joints with Home_joint every control cycle and writes it (1 even if the TCP is at Home_pose),
and it becomes 0 the moment the robot leaves home. When the task is not running this node manages it —
writing 0 when a jog is sent and 1 when move_home finishes. RCS moves the vehicle / lift only after
checking both this value and task_state (so the platform does not rise while the robot
is going home).
vehicle_ready (309) is the interlock in the opposite direction. RCS writes 1 when it confirms the vehicle has
stopped, the outriggers are locked and the lift has stopped, and 0 as soon as any of the three
starts moving. The robot task waits for this value to be 1 before moving (dus5_init) and
right before scanning (dus5_goto_zero) (state 290 = 14).
If it does not become 1 within about 2 minutes, the robot writes 299 = 8 and stops.
task_state (500) is the task state from the robot controller (1 running, 2 paused,
3 stopped). It is an input register, not holding, so it is read through the driver's fallback path.
Asking for the state via 29999 needs a command every time, so it is monitored here instead.
speed_scale (17) is the robot motion speed scale ratio [%] 2~100. It is read only
and not written — the setting is sent with 29999 'speed -v N'. Writing the register directly
also works, but the control path is kept in one place (29999).
work_area (256~261) is the grid information the robot uses to compute the arc. In order:
256 arc length [mm] 257 grid height [mm] 258 scanner height [0.1mm]
The 0.1 mm fields (258/260/261/262/263) hold values with decimals —
e.g. radius 834.6, effective coverage 167.5. Rounding to integer mm visibly distorts the arc shape and
the row spacing.
the arc shape is visibly distorted. kind=raw, so the node writes the value as an integer as is —
the 0.1 mm conversion is multiplied in beforehand by the sender (operator-ui).
259 minimum overlap [mm] 260 radius [0.1mm]  261 thickness [0.1mm]
262 probe effective width [0.1mm]  263 probe effective height [0.1mm]  (coverage actually inspected per pass: 5-axis cross 30x30 / 8-axis rectangle 75x167.5. The height is the max up step)
264 EOAT type (eoat_type)  0 = none 5 = 5-axis 8 = 8-axis
scan_go (267) is the scan start permission. When the robot reaches the origin it sets state (290) to 7
and waits until 1 arrives here. RCS sees state 7, tells ERUT the robot has arrived,
and writes 1 when ERUT sends the job start. The robot clears it to 0 itself when passing —
so a stale permission from the last cycle does not let it pass unchecked next time.
state 8 is the wetting (rubbing) phase — water is spread over the inspection surface right before the scan.
mark_target (268~269) is the marking spot. 268 = distance u [mm] along the arc from the origin,
269 = v [mm] up from the origin height. Read by dus_mark_point of the marking task.
marking task state (290): 10 moving, 11 against the wall (waiting for marking), 13 going home, 12 home reached = done.
mark_go (278) is the marking done signal. The marker belongs to ERUT, so the robot waits at 11,
and RCS writes 1 when ERUT sends req/mark_next. The robot clears it to 0 when passing.
299 = 5 means no wall contact was found at the marking spot.
The probes spread over the EOAT width, so the TCP does not need to go to the end of the grid —
the robot shortens the real travel to arc_run = arc length - EOAT width.
start_pose (316~321) is the tool flange pose when touching the work surface (as taught).
The EOAT centre offset (pendant variables eoat5_offset / eoat8_offset, [x,y,z] mm) is not used for robot
motion; it is used only to compute the scan coordinates (280~285, 286/287).
scan_arc (286/287) is the position on the arc during a scan. 286 = distance along the arc from the origin in this row
[0.1mm], 287 = accumulated up to the finished rows [mm]. Used to tell ERUT the actual inspection position (pos)
— the horizontal position in the grid is this value, the vertical is 291 (row number) x 296 (pitch, 0.1mm).
288/289 are the press state during a scan (0 not watched · 1 OK · 2 under-pressed (sensor lifted) · 3 over-pressed) and
that row's press correction [0.01mm] (read together with scan_arc since 2026-10-19). RCS raises E3002
PROBE_CONTACT_LOST if 288 stays 2 for more than 1 s — after a brief lift the robot presses back on its own.
probe_result (300~305) is the 3-point measurement result. 300/301/302 = X of the centre/origin (left)/right contact points
[0.1mm], 303 = extra advance at the centre to find the wall [0.1mm], 304/305 = number of attempts / contacts.
probe_poses (330~355) are those contact poses. 330~335 centre, 340~345 right, 350~355 origin
(position 0.1mm, rotation mrad), 346 = arc direction, 347~349 = probe centre offset [0.1mm].
The calibration (ERUT req/calibrate) moves these three points to the probe centre, fits a circle,
and reports the difference between its radius and the input radius (260+261) as calibration_error_mm.
Digital IO (0~3) are slots fixed by the controller (user manual 15.2 register mapping).
0 standard digital inputs  1 configurable inputs + tool IO  2 standard digital outputs  3 configurable outputs + tool IO
One register has 16 bits; bit 0 upwards maps to the IO numbers. These are output registers, so
both reading and writing work — the node reads register 2, changes one bit and writes it back (digital_out).
The water spray valve and the marker will also be attached here. They do not exist yet, so the numbers are undecided;
adding the DO number to the screen list (operator-ui config/plc_io.json) is enough to pick them up.
The task no longer multiplies by the speed ratio (307) — the controller applies the ratio received with 29999
'speed -v N' (multiplying in the script accumulated per cell and kept slowing down).

scale._comment: Real value per register count. Positions in mm, rotations in mrad.

write._standby_comment: 310~315 = scan standby pose joints (formerly home, 2026-10-16). With 308 (pose_src)=1 the task reads them as Standby_joint. 322~327 = home joints; with 328 (home_src)=1 the task reads them as Home_joint.
